newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati council voting on ticket tax increase.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati council voting on ticket tax increase.

text.p: Cincinnati City Council is expected to approve increasing the city ticket tax Wednesday partly to fund $100 million of bonds for the public schools, a council aide said.

The ticket tax increase from 3 percent to 4 percent would run from 1998 to 2006 to generate revenue for the Cincinnati general fund and the school building program, said Jeff Eichhorn, aide to Councilman Phil Heimlich.

Cincinnati and surrounding Hamilton County had pledged last year to provide $5 million each in annual revenues for school capital projects when seeking voter approval for a half-cent sales tax increase to finance two new professional sports stadiums.
City public schools would begin receiving the revenue when the first stadium opens, anticipated in 2000, Eichhorn said.
Cincinnati would meet its goals by using the ticket tax increase and revenues from the new football and baseball stadiums.

The ticket tax increase would last a maximum of nine years and could be retired in six or seven if revenue projections for the new stadiums hold true, said Jeff Berding, director of community affairs for the Cincinnati Bengals football team.

The Bengals are part of a coalition of entertainment groups that had earlier opposed a much higher proposed ticket tax increase. The coalition does not oppose the ticket tax plan to be voted on Wednesday, Berding said.
The Bengals stadium is scheduled to open before the 2000 football season while planning for the Cincinnati Reds ballpark continues.
